question_text: For an aluminum alloy under constant load, the creep rate increased by a factor of 2 when the temperature was increased from $71\,^\circ\text{C}$ to $77\,^\circ\text{C}$. Find the activation energy.The unit of the answer is kJ/mole.
response:
The creep rate follows the Arrhenius equation:

$$\dot{\varepsilon} = A\exp\!\left(-\frac{Q}{RT}\right)$$

Taking the ratio at the two temperatures (344 K and 350 K):

$$2 = \exp\!\left[\frac{Q}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1}-\frac{1}{T_2}\right)\right]$$

$$Q = \frac{R\ln 2}{\dfrac{1}{T_1}-\dfrac{1}{T_2}} = \frac{8.314\ln 2}{\dfrac{1}{344}-\dfrac{1}{350}} \approx 115{,}641\ \text{J/mol}$$

$$\boxed{115.6}$$
